messages.subject: Violin Plot - 6 lines of madness
parts:
Hi there,

I am trying to create a violin plot with ggplot2 (which looks awesome
by the way). I am probably not understanding the code correctly by
this is what I am trying (this works if you want to copy and paste it
in R)


library(ggplot2)
p <- rep(c(rep("condition_a", 4), rep("condition_b", 4)), 2)
q <- c(rep("grp_1", 8), rep("grp_2", 8))
r <- sample(1:5, 16, rep = T)
d <- data.frame(p, q, r)
gg1 <- ggplot(d, aes(y=r, x=factor(p)))
gg2 <- gg1 + geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = ..density.., ymin = -..density..),
stat = "density") + facet_grid(q ~ ., as.table = F, scales = "free_y")
+ labs(x = "some x desc", y = "some y desc")
print(gg2)


The result I am getting is posted as an image at
http://awesomescreenshot.com/0e8ae8c52
I tried to draw what I would like to achieve.

What I want is to draw traditional violin plots grouping them by
grp_1, grp_2 etc (so q above). For each group I have two conditions
(p above) which I want to plot violin plots for their values.
I want the plots to be vertical (as drawn in red in my image)

Any ideas on how to change the above code to do just that? I have
been playing with facet_grid all day...
Also the values on the axis are incorrect ... they should be in the
range 1:5 (as r above) and a plot should show the probability density
of that value...

Any help? I am going mad...

Many Thanks
JP

parts:
Hi:

I'm not sure whether or not this is what you're after, but here are a couple of options:

gg2 <- gg1 +
       geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = ..density.., ymin = -..density..),
                      stat = "density") +
       facet_grid(q ~ ., as.table = F, scales = "free_y") +

labs(x = "some x desc", y = "some y desc") + coord_flip()

gg3 <- ggplot(d, aes(x = factor(p), y = r)) +

geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = ..density.., ymin = -..density..),
                      stat = "density") +

facet_grid(. ~ q, as.table = F) +
       labs(x = "some x desc", y = "some y desc") + coord_flip()

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Violin Plot - 6 lines of madness
parts:
Hi:

As far as I can tell, this is a nontrivial problem in ggplot2 if you want the exact arrangement as shown in the lattice plot.  Here are some of the problems:

(1) geom_ribbon() is defined in terms of a ymin and a ymax. For a violin plot, this means the factor levels have to be on the vertical axis for the violin to be rendered. However, if you use the factor levels,

> ggplot(d, aes(x = r, y = p)) +
+       geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = ..density.., ymin = -..density..,
+                         fill = p), stat = 'density')
Error: Non-continuous variable supplied to scale_y_continuous.

# It requires p to be numeric. I added a variable s to d that is the numeric version of p and tried again:
d$s <- rep(rep(1:2, each = 4), 2)
ggplot(d, aes(x = r, y = s)) +
      geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = ..density.., ymin = -..density..,
                        fill = p), stat = 'density')

# The fill aesthetic is an attempt to 'break up' the condition_a and condition_b groups.
# The good news is that the fill color distinguishes the groups; the bad news is that
# they are both centered at zero, which follows because the two parts of the violin are centered at zero.

I tried using position_dodge in a couple of ways to separate condition_a and condition_b within a panel, but they weren't budging, perhaps because position_dodge may not be operative in geom_ribbon().

(2) It appears that part of the problem is trying to accommodate two factors. An example from the LearnR blog:
http://learnr.wordpress.com/2009/07/02/ggplot2-version-of-figures-in-lattice-multivariate-data-visualization-with-r-part-3/
(see Figure 3.14) shows that the x variable is the one for which the density is computed while the y variable is integer. One could use coord_flip() to interchange the x and y variables ex post facto, but the violins must be drawn as specified. Also notice there is only one grouping variable. When two grouping variables are used, one would like to be able to dodge the violins according to the levels of the second factor, but as the note at the end of (1) indicated, position_dodge had no effect.

If we combine the levels of p and q into one four level factor, we can get something that sort of resembles what you were after, but it's a compromise strategy:

d$pq <- with(d, paste(p, q))
ggplot(d, aes(x = r, y = as.numeric(pq))) +
geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = ..density.., ymin = -..density..),

fill = 'blue', alpha = 0.3, stat = 'density') +
      facet_wrap(~ pq, nrow = 1) + coord_flip() +
      opts(axis.text.x = theme_blank(), axis.ticks = theme_blank()) + ylab("")

Perhaps one of the experts can come up with a cleaner solution than this. It's always possible that I overlooked something.

HTH,
Dennis

library(ggplot2)
p <- rep(c(rep("condition_a", 4), rep("condition_b", 4)), 2)
q <- c(rep("grp_1", 8), rep("grp_2", 8))
r <- sample(1:5, 16, rep = T)
d <- data.frame(p, q, r)

ggplot(d, aes(x = r)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = ..density.., ymin =
-..density..), stat = "density") + facet_grid(q ~ p) + coord_flip()

= ..density.., ymin = -..density..), stat = "density") + facet_wrap( ~
q) + coord_flip()


Looks good to me...
